item.title: As Springfield s 15 000 Haitians brace for deportations local churches train to resist ICE
item.description: “We have orders of deportation,” said a volunteer in a raised voice, posing as an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent and pounding on the sanctuary door. “What you’re doing is harboring.” Inside the sanctuary, hundreds of trainees blocked the large wooden double doors. One called out, “We’re exercising our First Amendment right to freedom of worship.”

item.title: What we could not see as beautiful
item.description: “It’s trash, frankly.” So said the seasoned professor of German literature at the first Zoom meeting of the Catholic reading group I facilitated. She wasn’t the only one, either. Others were nicer about it, but it was clear that even the most open-minded of those who had assembled were being open-minded about a book they thought was pretty bad.

item.title: A better prayer for prisons
item.description: I spent my first 18 years in the General Association of Regular Baptist Churches and the next 30 wandering from denomination to denomination. In college I developed a romantic fixation on Catholicism and Orthodoxy, as disappointed evangelicals tend to do in college. I am denominationally postmodern.
